units.summary: The test now builds a two-step breaker so it matches the new groupBreaker type. It only changes the test's setup.
units.headline: Test uses two-step circuit breaker constructor
units.reason: Test-only constructor swap that follows the production type change and adds no new assertions.

units.summary: The test now builds a two-step breaker so it matches the new groupBreaker type. Only the test setup changes.
units.headline: Test uses two-step circuit breaker constructor
units.reason: Test-only constructor swap that follows the production type change.

units.summary: routerMetrics gains a longRunning gauge vector for watches, and its doc comment is updated. The struct is internal, but it changes which metrics the router exposes.
units.headline: routerMetrics gains a long-running watches gauge
units.reason: Adds an unexported metrics field. The behavior change is in instrument and newRouterMetrics, and the struct itself is low-risk.

units.summary: Watch requests are now counted in a per-group long-running gauge and are kept out of the in-flight gauge and the duration histogram. The histogram gains a verb label, which changes the metric's series and label set for dashboards and alerts. Watches are logged when they end.
units.headline: Watches tracked in separate gauge; histogram gains verb label
units.reason: It changes the label set of an exported metric and splits the control flow by verb, so dashboards and alerts are affected.
focus: dashboards or alerts that use http_request_duration_seconds without the verb label
watches that fail fast (503 or 4xx) are no longer in the duration histogram, so their errors are not visible
defer order: log, then gauge decrement, on watch end

units.summary: GrafanaRouter gets a router-wide watches context and cancel function. They are used to end all in-progress watches on shutdown.
units.headline: GrafanaRouter holds a router-wide watch cancellation context
units.reason: Adds lifecycle and cancellation state that affects shutdown and concurrency behavior.
focus: every constructor path initializes watches and endWatches
closeWatches is called on every stop path

units.summary: Upgrade requests to routed groups now get a 400. Watch requests run through serveWatch, scoped to their entry's watches context, so they end when the backend is replaced or the router closes.
units.headline: Routed watches get cancellable scope; upgrades rejected with 400
units.reason: It changes request handling and adds rejection of upgrades, so a reviewer needs to judge it.
focus: upgrade rejection happens before the breaker, so it does not count against it
a watch that starts against an already-retired entry ends immediately and the client reconnects to the new snapshot

units.summary: The unregistered-group fallback now rejects upgrade requests with a 400. It also runs watches through serveWatch with no group scope, so they end only on router shutdown.
units.headline: Fallback path rejects upgrades and wraps watches
units.reason: It changes request handling on the fallback path.
focus: standalone fallback clients that previously used websocket upgrades now get a 400
a nil scope is handled in serveWatch

units.summary: A new file with the request verb detection, upgrade rejection, serveWatch and closeWatches. serveWatch cancels a watch's context when its scope or the router ends. It swallows ErrAbortHandler panics when the router itself ended the watch, so the client sees a clean end.
units.headline: New watch lifecycle: scoped cancel, clean end, upgrade rejection
units.reason: It adds concurrency, context cancellation and panic recovery, and it rejects protocol upgrades.
focus: recover swallows only ErrAbortHandler when the router canceled and the client did not
requestVerb falls back to the lowercased HTTP method when RequestInfo parsing fails
Connection header detection in rejectUpgrade handles comma-separated values
closeWatches is called from the service stop path
